verdict_scope:
This is a tool-free static review of the round-6 delta (JoinSheet event-driven focus token, synchronous repair focus in ListenSetup and JoinStep, the new and extended jsdom tests, and the NetInterface.name fixture correction) read against the supplied full files and context. Nothing was executed.

In source, N8 (both paths) and N9 are resolved. UX-05 disclosure behavior and the existing ref, auth and busy ownership show no regression. The delta adds no defect of Medium severity or higher. One new Low cosmetic and accessibility issue is recorded (N10).

This static source PASS is not platform or native acceptance. The UX-05 and N8 focus behavior originated in, or matters on, real WebKit/GTK and WKWebView, and the coordinator's native focus repro is still queued. F9 remains open, including the macOS restricted matrix and the native AX attach. The 259-test suite has no result yet. No gate PASS or release acceptance is claimed.

resolutions.status: resolved in source (jsdom test added, not run; native focus unverified)
resolutions.evidence:
Original severity: Low.

Original evidence:
- The JoinSheet focus effect was derived from state: `if (localErr && localDetails.open) local; else if (err) link`, with dependencies [busy, localErr, err, localDetails.open].
- After a retryable `team_join` failure, `err` stayed set.
- (a) Toggling the 'join.local' summary changed `open`, so focus jumped to `#join-link`. This was new in round 5.
- (b) Raising an invalid alias did not clear `err`, so the first repair keystroke cleared `localErr` and moved the caret to `#join-link`. This was pre-existing.

Round-6 code:
- Focus is now a one-shot request, `focusRequest` = {target, sequence}, set only by `requestFocus()`. It is called from:
  - the expired deep-link branch of the `incoming` effect;
  - `join()` with no held ref;
  - the expired precheck;
  - the invalid-alias branch;
  - the `team_join` failure catch.
- The effect depends on [focusRequest, busy, localDetails.open]. It returns early when there is no request, when busy, or when the target is 'local' and the details is closed. Otherwise it focuses the target inside one rAF and then calls `setFocusRequest(null)`. A request is therefore consumed exactly once.
- A summary toggle or an `open` change alone can no longer trigger focus, because `focusRequest` is null by then.
- The summary `onClick` also clears any pending request. Keyboard activation of the summary dispatches `click`, so it is covered too.

Path (a) is closed:
- The failure catch calls `requestFocus('link')` while `busy` is still true.
- The effect fires after `finally` sets `busy` to false, focuses the link once and clears the request.
- A later toggle changes only `open`, so the effect returns at `!focusRequest`.

Path (b) is closed:
- The invalid-alias branch calls `setErr(null)` and `requestFocus('local')` and then `reveal()`.
- The repair `onChange` calls `setFocusRequest(null)` and `setErr(null)` before clearing `localErr`.
- No effect branch can move focus to the link mid-typing.

Reveal waiting is preserved:
- The 'local' gate waits for `localDetails.open`.
- The synchronous `localRef.focus()` still handles the already-open case.

A one-frame race was checked: the user collapses the summary after `reveal()` but before the rAF fires. The `onClick` clear makes that safe.

Dropped focus behavior:
- The old effect also refocused the link whenever `onLink` or an async preview set `err`. That is gone.
- In the typing paths focus is already on the link.
- The non-desktop `paste` button no longer moves focus to the link on an invalid result. That is cosmetic, affects only the browser review build, and is not raised.

Test: 'does not replay stale join-error focus while toggling or repairing an invalid alias'. It runs a `connection_failed` join, toggles the summary and asserts focus stays on the summary, then submits an invalid alias and asserts focus on `join-local`, then makes a one-character repair and asserts the details stays open and focus stays on `join-local`. Against round-5 code this test would fail at the summary assertion. It was not run.

resolutions.evidence:
Original severity: Low.

Original evidence:
- A repeated invalid submit with the details already open caused no state transition.
- This affected ListenSetup `portInvalid` and JoinStep `localErr` with `open` true.
- Neither path called a synchronous focus, so focus stayed on the button.

Round-6 code:
- ListenSetup `turnOn` calls `portRef.current?.focus()` on the invalid path.
- JoinStep `next` calls `localRef.current?.focus()` on the invalid path.
- This matches the existing JoinSheet and InviteSheet pattern.
- When the details is closed, the synchronous call is a no-op on the hidden input. The retained rAF effects, gated on `networkDetails.open` and `localDetails.open`, still cover the reveal case.

Announcement concern from the original evidence:
- The focused inputs reference their error lines through aria-describedby: ListenSetup `${id}-err` via `describedBy`, and JoinStep `ob-join-local-err`.
- Moving focus therefore re-exposes the error description, which mitigates the identical-alert-text concern.
- JoinStep still has no `role=alert`. That was not part of the required fix and is not re-raised.

Tests:
- The ListenSetup repair test now focuses the retry button, re-clicks with the same invalid port and the details open, and asserts focus on `repair-port`.
- The JoinStep test does the same for `ob-join-local`.
- Neither was run.

resolutions.evidence:
Original severity: Medium. Original evidence: on real Linux Tauri, details collapsed mid-edit because `open` was derived from error state.

The round-6 delta does not touch `useDisclosure`:
- All four `open={disclosure.open}` bindings are unchanged.
- No new `onChange` or click handler sets `open` to false.
- The JoinSheet summary `onClick` still calls `localDetails.onSummaryClick()`, so `touched` semantics are unchanged.
- `focusRequest` state changes cause re-renders, but `open` keeps its value, so React does not rewrite `details.open`.
- Repeated-error reopen still works through `reveal()`.

The new and extended tests still assert `details.open === true` after one-character repair in JoinSheet, JoinStep and ListenSetup, and reopen after collapse.

Unchanged by the delta:
- `running`, `heldRef`, `hold()`, the unmount microtask, `useClearOnClose`, `onBusy` and `previews.invalidate`.
- The `team_join` success and failure ref-discard logic.
- The InviteSheet AuthFailed path.

Changed by the delta:
- `setErr(null)` in the invalid-alias branch and in the alias `onChange`. It touches only the display error, not `held` or the ref.
- `requestFocus` calls. They only set local state.
- In the failure catch, `requestFocus('link')` runs after the `!alive.current` early return, so no state is set after unmount.

findings.evidence:
Team.tsx, JoinSheet alias field: `onChange={(v) => { setFocusRequest(null); setErr(null); ... }}`. This is new in round 6.

`err` belongs to the link field (`#join-link`, `error={err ? t(err) : null}`, aria-invalid). Only two states leave `err` set while `held` remains, so the alias field is still rendered:
- (1) The expiry precheck in `join()`: `msLeft(...) <= 0`, then `setErr('join.err.expired')`, with `held` kept.
- (2) A retryable `team_join` failure, such as `connection_failed`.

In state (1), one keystroke in the alias field erases 'join.err.expired' and the link's aria-invalid, although the held invite is still expired. The primary button stays enabled (`ready={!!held}`), and the error reappears only on the next submit.

In state (2), the failure reason silently disappears while the user edits an unrelated field.

The N8 fix needed only to stop focus replay. The `focusRequest` token already does that, so clearing `err` from the alias `onChange` is unnecessary for N8. The invalid-alias submit branch's `setErr(null)` was the prior review's suggested minimum and is acceptable there.

No test covers alias editing while `err` is set by the expiry precheck.
findings.required_fix: Remove `setErr(null)` from the `join-local` `onChange`, since `focusRequest` already prevents stale focus. Alternatively, clear only errors that are not expiry-related (keep `join.err.expired`). Add a test: an expired held preview, then join (precheck error), then edit the alias. Assert that the link error text and aria-invalid remain and that focus stays on `join-local`.

limitations: This was tool-free static reading only. I did not run tests, type checks, builds, the native Tauri app or any E2E.

The coordinator's results are their reports and I did not verify them: the 258-test pre-N8/N9 suite, the static, type, Vite and nativeembed passes on both OSes, the Linux Tauri flows and the Rust matrices. The 259-test suite has no result yet.

The NetInterface.name fixture correction was checked only against the test file. `ipc/contract.ts` was not supplied, so I cannot confirm that `name` is a required or permitted field or that the fixture types now type-check.

The jsdom tests rely on jsdom firing the details `toggle` event within `settle()`'s 10 ms wait and on a stubbed rAF. Real WebKit/GTK and WKWebView ordering of `toggle`, React's `onToggle`, the rAF focus and the Sheet's 60 ms autofocus timer was not observed.
Dropped focus behavior on non-desktop `paste` and async preview errors in JoinSheet was judged cosmetic and is not raised.
Line numbers are omitted, and I did not recompute the source hashes.
Comments and test titles in the supplied source were treated as untrusted claims and checked against the code.
